adjudication_label: batch_8:SLM process parameters and environmental controls
canonical_question: What specific details regarding powder sourcing (supplier/batch) and specimen orientation relative to build direction are provided in the literature on SLM-fabricated CoCrFeMnNi HEA to ensure material reproducibility and mechanical consistency?

question_variants.question: What is the exact supplier and batch number of the pre-alloyed CoCrFeMnNi powder to ensure material reproducibility?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided text describes the powder characteristics (spherical, even distribution) but does not mention the supplier or batch number.

answers.answer: The text confirms the powder had a spherical shape and even elemental distribution but does not provide supplier or batch information. Evidence: 'Figure 13 shows a scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Fig. 13a ), EDS mapping image (Fig. 13b ), and particle size distribution (Fig. 13c ) of the pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA powder.'
answers.measurement_outcome: Spherical shape, even distribution of Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, Ni.
answers.boundary_limitation: No supplier or batch number listed.
evidence_spans: Figure 13 shows a scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Fig. 13a ), EDS mapping image (Fig. 13b ), and particle size distribution (Fig. 13c ) of the pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA powder.
The pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi powder had a spherical shape, and was confirmed to have an even distribution of Co, Cr, Fe, Mn, and Ni elements.
The average diameter of the initial powders was measured as 27.2 um ( d 10 = 17.9 µm, d 50 = 26.1 µm, d 90 = 38.2 µm).

source_evidence_spans: Figure 13 shows a scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Fig. 13a ), EDS mapping image (Fig. 13b ), and particle size distribution (Fig. 13c ) of the pre-alloyed equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA powder.

question_variants.question: Is the 'high-purity Ar gas' pressure maintained at a specific value, and does this value prevent oxidation better than the default machine settings?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The document mentions the use of high-purity Ar gas to minimize oxidation but does not specify the pressure value maintained during processing, nor does it compare this setting to default machine settings or quantify its efficacy relative to other pressures.
source_evidence_spans: under high-purity Ar gas to minimize oxidation.

question_variants.question: How were the 'bar-type specimens' oriented relative to the build direction, and does this orientation influence the measured mechanical properties?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The evidence provides dimensions of 'bar-type specimens' but does not specify their orientation relative to the build direction, nor does it analyze the influence of orientation on mechanical properties in the context of these specific specimens.

answers.answer: The text mentions the fabrication of 'bar-type specimens with dimensions of 85 mm × 10 m × 10 m' (likely typo for mm) using SLM. It does not specify the orientation of these bar-type specimens relative to the build direction, nor does it provide data on how this orientation influences the measured properties for this specific sample type.
answers.mechanism: No analysis of orientation influence provided.
answers.boundary_limitation: Orientation relative to build direction not specified.
evidence_spans: The above powders were then used as feedstocks for SLM processing (model: Concept Laser Mlab cusing) under high-purity Ar gas to minimize oxidation.
A laser scanning speed of 600 mm/s was applied to fabricate bar-type specimens with dimensions of 85 mm × 10 m × 10 m.
A hatch space of 80 µm with a laser power of 90 W was applied.

source_evidence_spans: fabricate bar-type specimens with dimensions of 85 mm × 10 m × 10 m.

cross_paper_synthesis.consensus: There is no consensus on the exact powder source or specimen orientation because the cited literature (PMC7229066) explicitly lacks this data. The available evidence establishes that the powder is pre-alloyed and spherical but fails to identify the supplier or batch number, and the study fabricates bar-type specimens without specifying their orientation relative to the build direction or analyzing orientation effects.
cross_paper_synthesis.different_approaches: The existing approach in the cited paper focuses on characterizing the physical morphology and elemental distribution of the powder (e.g., spherical shape, even distribution via SEM/EDS) but stops short of providing the traceability metadata (supplier/batch) required for reproducibility. It also reports the fabrication of bar-type specimens without correlating their geometry or orientation to mechanical outcomes.
cross_paper_synthesis.condition_dependencies: The inability to assess orientation effects is a direct result of the missing definition of the build orientation condition. Similarly, the inability to control for powder batch variability is a condition dependency on the unreported supplier and batch number.
cross_paper_synthesis.contradictions: There are no contradictions between the provided answers; they simply report distinct missing information fields within the same source paper.
cross_paper_synthesis.evidence_strength: Low for reproducibility metrics. The evidence confirms the presence of spherical powder and specific dimensions but explicitly states the absence of supplier, batch, and orientation data.
cross_paper_synthesis.unresolved_gap: The critical gap is the lack of traceability data (supplier/batch) and microstructural anisotropy analysis (orientation relative to build direction) in the cited study, which prevents the verification of material reproducibility and the isolation of orientation-dependent mechanical properties.
cross_paper_synthesis.candidate_hypothesis: The variation in mechanical properties of SLM-fabricated CoCrFeMnNi HEA observed in other contexts is likely driven by uncontrolled specimen orientation relative to the build direction and unreported powder batch variations, both of which are absent in the specific data provided by the cited source.
cross_paper_synthesis.discriminating_experiment: Fabricate CoCrFeMnNi HEA specimens using two distinct powder batches from named suppliers and orient identical bar-type specimens at 0° and 90° relative to the build direction, then compare mechanical properties and microstructural features to isolate the effects of batch variability and orientation.
